newsitem.title: UK: Williams sells 15 businesses in MBO.
newsitem.headline: Williams sells 15 businesses in MBO.

text.p: British conglomerate Williams Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it was selling 15 of its heating, construction and home products businesses in a management buyout (MBO) for 360 million pounds ($600.5 million) in cash.

Williams will retain a 26 percent stake in the MBO, which will be called Newmond Ltd and covers activities including the Swish curtain track business and Rawlplug construction and home improvement products.

"This sale clearly demonstrates our commitment to focusing on businesses with international growth potential. The proceeds will provide the group with substantial additional resources with which to strengthen and develop our international positions in fire protection, security products and home improvement products," Williams Chairman Sir Nigel Rudd said in a statement.
The MBO will be led by Mike Davies, who will resign as a director of Williams, and is in partnership with Candover Partners Ltd.

Williams expects to make an exceptional gain of some 246 million pounds on the sale, less goodwill of 156 million, and expects a small dilution in earnings before any reinvestment of the proceeds. It will invest 57 million pounds in Newmond.

Separately, Williams said it was pleased with the group's overall performance in the second half, recognising that while favourable conditions prevailed in the U.S. and some improvement was seen in Britain, European markets remained difficult. ($1=.5995 Pound)
